attempts.summary: Implemented cross-LAN firewall using Ansible run from node4 (the cluster's Ansible controller). node1 (VyOS) routes between lan-a (eth1, 10.50.10.0/24, node2) and lan-b (eth2, 10.50.20.0/24, node3). VyOS forward-filter firewall: rule 10 accepts established/related, rule 20 accepts TCP/5432 from eth1→eth2 (node2→node3), rules 30/40 explicitly reject all other eth1↔eth2 traffic in both directions, default-action drop as backstop (VyOS's default-action leaf only supports drop/accept, not reject, so explicit reject rules cover the "reject all other traffic" requirement). Verified end-to-end: TCP/5432 node2→node3 succeeds; other ports, ICMP, and the reverse direction on 5432 are all rejected with ICMP port-unreachable. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all 4 nodes (node1 VyOS, node2, node3, node4) one at a time — captured boot_id baselines, restarted each via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified recovery (interfaces, routes, firewall rules, and actual TCP/ICMP behavior all intact after reboot). Discovered and fixed a persistence gap: node1's ad-hoc ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for the vyos user did not survive VyOS's reboot (not part of its config-store persistence), so re-added the cluster SSH key via VyOS's native `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config path, which does persist; re-ran the Ansible playbook afterward to confirm full idempotent success across all three managed hosts.
